walkthroughs.body_html:
Fields — a core area of Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Fields brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Fields.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Field strength relates to potential by:
options: E = +dV/dr
E = -dV/dr
E = V/r only
E = Vr

mcqs.q: Capacitance of parallel plate capacitor depends on:
options: Charge stored only
Voltage applied only
Area, separation, permittivity
Resistance of wires

mcqs.q: What distinguishes gamma rays from X-rays of the same frequency?
options: Origin — gamma rays come from nuclear processes; X-rays come from electron transitions or deceleration of charged particles.
Gamma rays are slower than X-rays.
Gamma rays have higher frequency than any X-ray.
The nucleus shrinks to half its original size after one half-life.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the activity of a source and the dose received by a person?
options: Activity (Bq) is the rate of nuclear decays in the source; dose (Sv) measures the biological effect of absorbed radiation on tissue.
Gamma rays are slower than X-rays.
Activity is for nuclear power stations and dose is for medical X-rays.
Activity and dose are the same — both measure how dangerous the radiation is.
